from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Light travels as an oscillating wave.", "Superposition creates constructive interference peaks.", "Phase encodes the information."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Wave Nature of Light", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create elements
        source = Dot(color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(source, 'C2', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Animations
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        waves = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.1 + i * 0.2, color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=2) for i in range(5)])
        waves.move_to(source.get_center())
        self.play(FadeIn(source))
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[Create(w) for w in waves], run_time=2))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        slits = VGroup(Line(UP*0.5, DOWN*0.5, color=YELLOW), Line(UP*0.5, DOWN*0.5, color=YELLOW))
        self.place_in_area(slits, 'B5', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(slits))
        
        interference = Dot(color=PINK)
        self.place_at_grid(interference, 'C6', scale_factor=1.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(PINK))
        self.play(FadeIn(interference))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Mechanism of Diffraction", ["Light spreads upon hitting obstacles.", "Huygens-Fresnel principle defines this scattering.", "Diffraction is an object's signature."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Place a point light source (white)
        light_source = Dot(color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(light_source, 'C2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(light_source))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate plane waves (cyan) hitting an obstacle
        obstacle = Line(start=self.grid['B4'], end=self.grid['E4'], color=GREY, stroke_width=6)
        waves = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.5 + i*0.5, color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=2) for i in range(3)])
        waves.move_to(light_source.get_center())
        
        self.play(Create(obstacle))
        self.play(Create(waves))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show waves bending around obstacle edges (orange)
        bent_waves = VGroup(*[Arc(radius=0.5 + i*0.5, angle=PI/2, color=ORANGE, stroke_width=2) for i in range(3)])
        bent_waves.shift(obstacle.get_center() + RIGHT * 0.5)
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(waves, bent_waves))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Recording the Hologram (The Interference Pattern)", [
            "Split laser into two beams.",
            "Reference and Object beams interact.",
            "Interference pattern forms on film.",
            "This acts as complex grating.",
            "Grid stores 3D object data."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        film = Rectangle(width=2, height=3, color=GRAY).set_fill(WHITE, opacity=0.3)
        ref_beam = Line(LEFT*2, RIGHT*2, color=BLUE)
        obj_beam = Line(DOWN*2, UP*2, color=GREEN)
        obj = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        fringes = VGroup(*[Line(LEFT*0.5, RIGHT*0.5, color=WHITE).shift(UP*i*0.2) for i in range(-5, 6)])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Split laser into two beams.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(ref_beam, 'B2', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(obj_beam, 'E4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(ref_beam), Create(obj_beam))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Reference and Object beams interact.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(obj, 'E2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_in_area(film, 'B3', 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(obj), FadeIn(film))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Interference pattern forms on film.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.play(FadeIn(fringes.move_to(film.get_center())))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # This acts as complex grating.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(fringes.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.5))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Grid stores 3D object data.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(RED)
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Reference beam strikes developed hologram.",
            "Diffraction reconstructs original wavefronts.",
            "Floating 3D ghost appears.",
            "Light mimics the object source.",
            "Visual depth is perfectly preserved."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Reconstruction: Decoding the Diffraction", lecture_lines)
        
        # Mobjects
        hologram = Rectangle(width=2, height=3, color=GRAY, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(hologram, 'D3')
        
        ref_beam = Line(start=np.array([-4, 1, 0]), end=hologram.get_left(), color=BLUE)
        diffracted_light = VGroup(*[Line(hologram.get_right(), np.array([4, 1 + i*0.5, 0]), color=YELLOW) for i in range(-2, 3)])
        ghost_image = Circle(radius=0.5, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(ghost_image, 'C5')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(Create(ref_beam))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(diffracted_light))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(FadeIn(ghost_image))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Holography stores complex diffraction patterns.", "Secures credit card data.", "Enables advanced AR displays."]
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Real-World Application", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        hologram_icon = Dot(color=RED, radius=0.4)
        self.place_at_grid(hologram_icon, 'C3')
        self.play(FadeIn(hologram_icon), Indicate(hologram_icon), run_time=1.5)
        self.lecture[0].set_color(RED)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        card = Rectangle(color=PURPLE, width=3, height=2)
        card_label = Text("Credit Card", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(card, DOWN)

        self.play(FadeIn(card_group), run_time=1.5)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(PURPLE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        ar_glass = Ellipse(color=YELLOW, width=2, height=1)
        self.place_at_grid(ar_glass, 'B5')
        self.play(Create(ar_glass), run_time=1.5)

        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Principles of Holography and Diffraction: Capturing Light in 3D

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Wave Nature of Light
sections.content: Briefly review wave superposition and phase coherence. Explain that light acts as a wave (y = A sin(kx - ωt + φ)), emphasizing that interference patterns encode information about phase, not just intensity.
sections.example: Visualizing ripples in a pond merging: when two peaks meet, they create a 'super-peak' (constructive interference).

sections.title: The Mechanism of Diffraction
sections.content: Explain the Huygens-Fresnel principle. Diffraction occurs when light waves encounter an obstacle/aperture, causing them to spread. This scattering is the 'signature' of the object's geometry.
sections.example: Laser light passing through a tiny slit on a screen, creating a distinct light-and-dark fringe pattern rather than a single point.

sections.title: Recording the Hologram (The Interference Pattern)
sections.content: Show the optical setup: a laser split into a 'Reference Beam' and an 'Object Beam'. The interaction on the recording plate captures the interference fringes, which act as a complex diffraction grating.
sections.example: A 3D model of a 'Cyber-Robot' reflecting light to meet a direct reference beam, creating a chaotic-looking but highly detailed grid on the film.

sections.title: Reconstruction: Decoding the Diffraction
sections.content: Explain that when the original reference beam strikes the developed hologram, it diffracts off the recorded interference pattern, reconstructing the original wavefronts emitted by the object.
sections.example: Shining a flashlight at a flat 'Dragon Sculpture' hologram, which projects a perfect, floating 3D light-ghost of the dragon in mid-air.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Application
sections.content: Synthesize the process: Holography is essentially 'storing diffraction patterns.' Discuss applications in secure data storage, medical imaging, and augmented reality glasses.
sections.example: Using holographic labels on credit cards to prevent forgery, where the tilt of the card reveals different diffraction depths.
